title: A functor carries a retract to a retract
statement: Let $\mathcal C$, $\mathcal D$ be categories, $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ a functor, and $X,Y$ objects of $\mathcal C$ with morphisms $\iota:X\to Y$ and $\rho:Y\to X$ such that $\rho\circ\iota=\mathrm{id}_X$ ($X$ is a retract of $Y$). Then $F(\rho)\circ F(\iota)=\mathrm{id}_{F(X)}$: $F(X)$ is a retract of $F(Y)$, with section $F(\iota)$ and retraction $F(\rho)$. (No additivity of $F$ is needed.)

source.place: Etale Cohomology, Lemma 0A4C (label lemma-sandwich), proof, first paragraph ("Since $\mathcal I$ is injective we see that $\mathcal I$ is a direct summand of $f_*\mathcal J$. Thus it suffices to prove the desired vanishing for $f_*\mathcal J$"): the step left implicit by "Thus"
